definitions.explanation: An informal, familiar term for one's wife or someone else's wife. Primarily used by men in casual conversation.

examples.japanese: かみさんに{聞|き}いてみるよ。
かみさんの{手料理|てりょうり}が{一番|いちばん}うまい。
examples.english: My wife's home cooking is the best.

examples.japanese: うちのかみさんが{怒|おこ}ると{怖|こわ}いから、{早|はや}く{帰|かえ}らないと。
examples.english: My wife is scary when she's angry, so I'd better get home early.

notes:
USAGE:
Used mainly by middle-aged and older men to refer to their own wife in casual settings. It has a down-to-earth, familiar tone. Not appropriate in formal situations, where {妻|つま} or {家内|かない} would be used instead.

The word comes from {上|かみ}さん, originally a respectful term for a woman of higher status or the lady of the house.

REGISTER:
Informal and spoken. Common among working-class and older male speakers. Younger men tend to prefer {奥|おく}さん (for others' wives) or {妻|つま} (for their own).
